- When sentiment shows strong positive spikes (e.g., 1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 3–8% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.33 or 0.00) after a peak, model continues upward — force mean reversion toward recent 5-day average.
- When true outcome drops sharply after a forecast peak, model fails to anticipate — adjust forecast downward by 10–15% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If model consistently overpredicts in early forecast window (e.g., first 5–7 days), reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is flat or mixed (0.00/0.33), model tends to overfit recent history — use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome shows early decline after a peak, model often ignores it — apply early correction rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% at 10–15 day mark if sentiment turns negative.
